decision: Use received_at as the knowledge clock with a 07:45 as-of cut-off; late-arriving pings kept for reconciliation only. The agent flagged the V-04 90-min lag; I set the rule.
quote: The clock I will use is `received_at`, which will tell me what information was known to the server.

decision: Define late as progress along route vs schedule; Mon/Tue as secondary check; promised ETA tracked separately, not as lateness.
quote: Latency will be determined by comparing the actual progress of the bus along its journey at the time against that which is expected according to schedule. The schedule will act as the main yardstick.

decision: Reject both rev. C rules: Route 12 not forced to 0, operator 7 kept. The agent recommended rejecting them; I agreed and set the NO_VERDICT fallback for operator 7.
quote: I reject both sets of Rev. C rules of reconciliation.

decision: 10 min of telemetry silence during a trip triggers CALL_DRIVER, as initial policy.
quote: 10 minutes of telemetry silence will be the first threshold for CALL_DRIVER during a trip.

decision: Overrode the agent's PUSH_LATE 58 min on Route 11: a bus stationary at origin gets NO_VERDICT ORIGIN_STATIONARY.
quote: For Route 11, I am not going to use the PUSH_LATE status.

decision: Overrode my own silence rule's CALL_DRIVER for Route 14: an ingestion delay is NO_VERDICT TELEMETRY_INGESTION_DELAY, escalated to telemetry, not the driver.
quote: This trip should be categorized as NO_VERDICT with TELEMETRY_INGESTION_DELAY reason, and escalated to the telemetry/operations team.

decision: Kept the agent's 5-min push threshold but added gates: on the way, reliable data, known before the cut-off.
quote: But, merely crossing this threshold will not suffice to set off a PUSH_LATE.

decision: Accepted the agent's worry-order but assigned a different owner per route (ops / driver / telemetry / rider push).
quote: This ordering of the concern hierarchy is appropriate, with one exception: Route 11 and Route 17 need a different approach to operations.

decision: Supersedes the Route 14 TELEMETRY_INGESTION_DELAY entry above: that verdict relied on 145 pings received after 07:45 (hindsight). Live, Route 14 and Route 17 get the same rule (CALL_DRIVER TELEMETRY_SILENT); the delivery-delay finding moves to the separate retrospective output. The agent found the leak during the audit; I set the requirement.
quote: Route 14 and Route 17 must be treated consistently when their available telemetry is silent.
